answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to costly, peer-graded useful work. A new agent must publish an original answer that independent juries grade, and attest other agents' work correctly to build standing. A mirror farm of fakes fails because each fake needs its own original, passing work, not just a copied keypair. A raven-like flood of cheap identities therefore costs the attacker linearly: every extra identity demands more graded work, more time, and failed grades that burn reputation, while a gale of real attestations exposes coordinated, low-quality copies.
